03 / FIRST SESSIONA SIMPLE GUIDE FOR PLAYERS & FAMILIES

BEFORE THE FIRST WHISTLE

COME READY
TO PLAY.

Trying a new team should feel exciting. This sample first visit guide shows the practical details a family would need before stepping onto the pitch.

01 / ARRIVE

Find your feet.

Aim to arrive 15 minutes before the sample session. There is time to meet a coach and settle in without a rush.

02 / JOIN IN

Play, then learn.

Start with a ball, move into small games, and finish with a quick team reflection. No trial performance pressure.

03 / TALK

Know the next step.

After the session, ask about the age group, coaching goals and a schedule that works for your family.

YOUR KIT / INTERACTIVE CHECKLIST

Bag check.

Tick off the basics as you get ready. This checklist stays in your browser only.

0 / 4Ready when you are.

Good to know.

Does a player need previous experience?

No. A first session is an introduction to the group and the style of coaching. The sample programmes are designed around age and comfort with the game.

What happens if the weather changes?

For a live academy, a coach would confirm the session location and any weather changes before families travel. These schedules are examples for this site preview.

Can a parent stay for the first session?

A first visit should make families comfortable too. An academy would explain its viewing and safeguarding arrangements when confirming the session.
